findings.title: Feature-flagged table widgets discard the query result
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, this branch renders `TableWidgetVisualization` with hard-coded empty `columns` and an empty `tableData` object rather than `fields`, `result.data`, and `result.meta`. Consequently every flagged dashboard table is blank regardless of the query result (and no loading/error behavior from the existing table is preserved). Pass the actual result data and metadata into the new visualization before enabling this path.

findings.title: Error IDs can be paired with the wrong nodestore records
findings.body: `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a mapping keyed by node ID and can omit records that are missing. Zipping the original `error_ids` with `events.values()` assumes both identical ordering and one value per requested ID. If any requested event is absent, all later IDs can be paired with another event's title/message/timestamp, causing the AI summary to receive incorrect error context. Look up each generated node ID explicitly and retain its associated error ID instead of consuming mapping values positionally.

findings.title: Browser report timestamp/age invariants are not enforced for zero values or absent fields
findings.body: Both `age` and `timestamp` are optional, and the mutual-exclusion validators test `self.initial_data.get(...)`. A report containing `age: 0` and `timestamp: 0` passes because both values are falsey; a report containing neither also passes. This accepts malformed reports despite the stated requirement to support one of the two spec formats, and allows ambiguous data to enter metrics processing. Check field presence (`"age" in initial_data` / `"timestamp" in initial_data`) and add object-level validation requiring exactly one of the two fields.
